intended_object: The decomposition map A/I → ⨁_i (A_i + I)/I of the natural grading on the quotient of a graded commutative ring A by a homogeneous ideal I. It sends [x] to ([x_i])_i. This comes from the docstring and from its use as `decompose'` in `gradedDecomposition` and `gradedRing`.
explanation: The body decomposes x ∈ A into its homogeneous components with `decomposeAddEquiv`, sends each component to its image in A/I, and lifts this map to A/I via `QuotientAddGroup.lift`. The lift is well defined because homogeneity of I (`hI.mem_iff`) puts every component of an element of I in I. The file proves this map is a two-sided inverse of the summation map `DirectSum.coeAddMonoidHom`, so it is exactly the canonical decomposition of the image grading. Commutative rings with an index set that is an additive monoid, and components given through `SetLike`, is the standard generality for this construction. A search of Mathlib at this commit found no grading on a quotient by a homogeneous ideal, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
